2.1 The tolerance on dimensions of working ends shall conform to 'fine* class of deviation and the 
tolerance on remaining dimensions shall conform tD medium' class of deviation of IS : 21 02 
( Part 1 )-1 980 'Qeneral tolerances tor dimensions and form arid position: Part 1 General 
tolerances for linear and angular dimensions { second revision )'. 

3. Material 

3.1 W/re — Stainless steal conforming to Designation 09Cr18Ni9 OT 04CM8NJ10 of fS : 6528- 
T972 'Specification for sfamtess s(eef wire'. 

3.2 Sheet — Stainless steel conforming to Designation 04Cr1 8Ni1Q or 07Cr18Ni9 of IS : 6911- 
1972 'Specification for stainless steel plate, sheet and strip'. 

4. Requirements 

4.1 The probes shall be free from burrs, pits, cracks, feathers, nicks a n d waviness when examined 
under 25 x magnification. All surfaces shall be free from pores, crevices and grinding marks. 



4.1.1 The instrument 
and polishing materials,

shall be supplied free from residual scale, acid, grease, and grinding

5. Passivation ami Final Treatment — The instruments shall be treated by a suitable 
passivation process. 

Not* — Examples of methods of passivacion are by efectropolishing or by treating wuh 10 percent ( v/« ) 

nitric acid solution for not less than 30 mm at a temperature of not lea* than 10*C and not exceeding 60°C 

The instruments should then be rinsed in water and dried in hot air. 

6- Surface Finish — The surface finish shall be one of or a combination of the following: 

a) Mirror polished; 

b) Reflection-reducing, for example, satin finish, matt black finish; and 

c) An applied surface coating, for example, for insulation purposes. 

Note 1 — The satin finish should be eFfacred by an appropriate procedure, such as grinding, brushing, 
elecHo polishing and, in addition, satin finishing (glass beading or satin brushing). The finish should be 
uniform and smooth and ir should reduce glare. 

Note 2 — Instruments of mirror finish should be adequately giound to remove all surface impsrfecliona and 
polished to remove giinding marks, resulting in a mirror finish. The miTror finish should be effected by an 
appropriate procedure, such as polishing, brushing, electropolishing and mirror buffing. 

7. Corrosion Resistance Test — The probes shall be tested in accordance with IS : 7531-1975 
'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless steel surgical 
instruments'. The probes shall show no sign of corrosion after the test. 

8. Sampling and Criteria for Conformity — A suitable sampling scheme and criteria for 
acceptance is given in Appendix A. 

9. Marking — Each probe sha/l be legibly marked with the manufacturer's name, initials or 
recognized trade-mark and its size. 

9.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

10. Packing — As agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



APPENDIX A 

( Cfause 3 ) 

SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

A-1- Lot — In any consignment, all the instruments produced from the same material under 
similar conditions shall constitute a lot. 

A-2. The number of instruments to be selected from each lot shall depend upon the size of the lot 
and shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 

* ^ ^_^^^^^ 

TABLE 1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 
Lot Size Sample Size 

(D <2) 

Up lo 15 2 

16 lo 50 3 

51 fo 150 5 

151 and above 8 

A-2-1 These instruments shall be selected from the lot at random and in order to ensure the 
randomness of selection, procedure given in IS : 4905-1968 'Methods of random sampling* may 
be followed. 

A-3. Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity — AU the instruments selected at random 
' in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1 shall be tested for shape and dimensions, material, 
requirements, surface finish, and corrosion resistance. The instruments shall be considered as 
defective- if it fails to meet any one of these requirements, A lot shall be considered as Conform- 
ing to these requirements if none of the instruments' in the sample is found to be defective in any 
of these tests. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard was first published in 1979 The present revision has been taken up to include 

certain modifications in order to bring the specification in line with the modern manufacturing 

practices. Accordingly, the tolerance clause covering the reference of concerned Indian Standard, 

material and requirements have ^een modified. Clauses on surface finish, passivation and final 

'treatment and sampling plan hatfe been added.
